A1.justification: Both PDFs describe The Counting Power of Transformers. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original transformer classification experiments on L_k for k = 1–5, including validation loss, test accuracy, and length-generalization results in Figure 1.

after.justification: v3 retains these experiments in Figure 2 and adds original experiments on five L_i,j languages in Appendix D and Figure 4.

M1.justification: The polynomial construction, ReLU multiplication gadget, uniform attention, and trained NoPE classifiers remain the same. v3 clarifies the gadget's layer composition and the theoretical models' single-head convention without introducing a new procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds five tasks from L_i,j = {a^m b^n c^(m^i n^j) : m,n >= 1}. These introduce a third symbol and exact multiplicative count constraints beyond the retained two-symbol L_k inequalities. The new language family also specifies fixed token order, although order-violating negative examples are not documented.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated competing methods against the transformer classifiers. C-RASP, SVMs, and other transformer classes are theoretical or contextual comparisons, not empirical baselines in the result tables.

E3.justification: The original training settings move from v2 Appendix D to v3 Section 6 unchanged: 500,000 training examples, one epoch, the same architecture grid and optimizer settings, and evaluation at lengths up to 500 and 501–1000. The added experiments explicitly reuse this setup; no distinct evaluation protocol is specified.

E4.justification: v3 extends the length-generalization analysis to the new L_i,j tasks, comparing in-distribution performance with performance on longer strings. This adds robustness evidence, particularly the larger generalization gap for L_3,3, without adding component ablations or a new sensitivity study.

E5.justification: Both versions report best-observed losses and accuracies without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional result rows retain this reporting practice.

E6.justification: Every original numerical entry is unchanged between v2 Figure 1 and v3 Figure 2. New Figure 4 substantially extends the findings to L_i,j: all five test accuracies are 0.99, while length-generalization accuracies range from 0.85 to 0.99; L_3,3 has generalization loss 2.26 and accuracy 0.85. These are additional task results, not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The principal theorems and appendix proofs are retained. v3 adds remarks asserting applicability under logarithmic rational precision and an O(dM) embedding-dimension bound, while reiterating the existing depth bound. It also corrects the temperature-scaled softmax denominator from exp(x_j tau) to exp(x_j/tau).

C1.justification: The semialgebraic expressivity, characterization, universality, and undecidability contributions remain unchanged. v3 adds introductory and concluding claims connecting the results to polynomial approximation of continuous token-count functions and potential NLP similarity and Zipf-related tasks.

C2.justification: v3 develops concrete NLP applicability arguments and explicitly excludes GeLU and SwiGLU from its analysis. Appendix D also qualifies the connection between expressivity and learnability, calling for focused study after observing weaker performance on longer inputs. v2 mainly emphasized successful learning and attributed performance variation to experimental limitations.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly documents the theoretical single-head convention and specifies one ReLU layer plus one attention layer per multiplication gadget, refining v2's less precise wording. Existing empirical hyperparameters are relocated rather than newly disclosed. No code, data access, or hardware information is added.

R1.justification: v3 extends the existing positioning with discussions of finite-precision characterizations and UHAT/C-RASP verification, citing works including Li and Cotterell (2025), Yang et al. (2025, 2026), and Bergsträßer et al. (2026). It also adds precision, text-similarity, and Zipf references. The central comparison with linear counting frameworks remains.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized prose and terminology corrections, adds an overview of the multiplication construction, and expands the concluding discussion. Training details move into Section 6, and Appendix D becomes Further Experimental Validation. The main section sequence and proof organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds a theoretical inclusion diagram as Figure 1 and the new performance table/plot as Figure 4. The original performance and proof diagrams remain as Figures 2 and 3. The performance caption clarifies loss/accuracy notation and removes the incorrect reference to bars; the underlying original line plot is unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 improves accessibility through the construction overview and result diagram, corrects the softmax formula, and adds empirical coverage with a more qualified learnability discussion. The central proofs and original scores remain unchanged, so the gain is limited. The new ordered-language experiments retain an unclear validation scope because their NoPE setup does not explain how order-violating negative examples are handled.
